title: 2023年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change.

P2 Supermarkets can technically be defined as giants housing 15,000 to 60,000 different products. The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America. There is some debate about which was the very first, but over the years a consensus has built around King Kullen Supermarket, founded in New York in 1930.

P3 For some 300 years, Americans had fed themselves from small stores and public markets. Shopping for food involved mud, noisy chickens, clouds of flies, nasty smells, bargaining, and getting short-changed. The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food. Supermarkets may not feel cutting-edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time. They were such strange marvels that, on her first official state visit to the United States in 1957, Queen Elizabeth II insisted on an impromptu(即兴的) tour of a suburban-Maryland Giant Food.

P4 The typical supermarket layout has barely changed over the past 90 years. Most stores open with flowers, fruit and vegetables at the front as a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite. Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you'll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way.

P5 In the early days, as the supermarket multiplied, so did our suspicion of it. We have long feared that this "revolution in distribution" uses corporate black magic on our appetite. The book The Hidden Persuaders, published in 1957, warned that supermarkets were putting women in a "hypnoidal trance(催眠恍惚状态)," causing them to wander aisles bumping into boxes and "picking things off shelves at random."

questions.q: What problem have supermarkets been facing?
options: They are actually on the way to bankruptcy.
They have been losing customers and profits.
They are forced to use e-commerce strategies.
They have difficulty adapting to climate change.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What problem have supermarkets been facing? 直接问一个具体事实——超市在面 临什么难处，答案应能在原文找到明确对应句。 46. What problem have supermarkets been facing? A) They are actually on the way to bankruptcy. B) They have been losing customers and profits. C) They are forced to use e-commerce strategies. D) They have difficulty adapting to climate change.

【拆句】What problem have supermarkets been facing? 是一个 what 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 是"超市一直在面对什么难处"，have been facing 是现在完成进行时，强调"长期、持续"在 面对，这个时态暗示原文会有 long/for more than a decade 一类的长期信号词，结构本 身无陷阱。

【定位】Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change. 长期以来，超市一直是利润最薄的行业之一，也是人们最不愿去工作或光顾的场所之一。十 多年来，它们一直受到电商巨头的攻击，被指责让美国人发胖，还被指控加剧气候变化。

【选项】A) 过度推断 原文只说超市利润薄、处境难，从未说它"正走向破产"；on the way to bankruptcy 把"利润薄"夸大成"濒临破产"，程度严重超出原文。 B) ✓ 正确 thinnest-margined businesses ↔losing customers and profits under attack from e-commerce giants ↔losing customers 预判落在"生意难做、客流利润受损"，四个选项里只有 They have been losing customers and profits. 同时覆盖了原文的"利润薄"和"受电商攻击"，与预判最契合。 C) 偷换概念 原文说超市"受电商攻击"，并没说它们"被迫去采用电商策略"；forced to use e- commerce strategies 把"被攻击"偷换成"被迫效仿"，是原文未提的内容。 D) 偷换概念 原文是超市"被指责加剧气候变化"（超市是被指责方），而 have difficulty adapting to climate change 说成"超市难以适应气候变化"，把"被指责制造问题"换成了"自己适应 不了"。 文章对自助式杂货店这一理念有何评价? A) 它是由King Kullen提出的。 B) 它起源于美国。 C) 它一直处于持续争论之中。 D) 它即使在今天也被证明是革命性的。

questions.q: What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery?
options: It was put forward by King Kullen.
It originated in the United States.
It has been under constant debate.
It proves revolutionary even today.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery? 问的是原文 就这个想法"说了什么"，是对原文具体陈述的核对，属细节题。 47. What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery? A) It was put forward by King Kullen. B) It originated in the United States. C) It has been under constant debate. D) It proves revolutionary even today.

【拆句】What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery? 主干是"原文关于 这个想法说了什么"，of the idea of a self-service grocery 是层层嵌套的 of 介词短语作后 置定语，只是在限定"哪个想法"，剥掉修饰后主干很清楚，无理解陷阱。

【定位】The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America. 让人们能在货架间自行寻找采集食物、而不必请店员从柜台后取货的自助式杂货这一革命性 想法，最早出现在美国。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 原文说金库伦是公认的"第一家超市"，并未说这个"想法"是金库伦"提出"的；put forward by King Kullen 把"第一家店"错安成"想法的提出者"。 B) ✓ 正确 first came about in America ↔It originated in the United States. 预判核心是"起源地是美国"，四项里只有 It originated in the United States. 准确对应 定位句的起源信息，故锁定。 C) 偷换概念 原文 some debate about which was the very first 争论的是"哪家是第一家店"，而 非"这个想法本身"；under constant debate 把争论对象由"谁是第一家"偷换成"这个 想法"。 D) 与原文相反 原文只说该想法当年是 revolutionary，并称超市 may not feel cutting-edge now （如今未必前沿），并无"至今仍具革命性"之说；proves revolutionary even today 是 原文没有的论断。 超市通过采用福特主义工厂方式做了什么? A) 它们在许多方面使传统杂货店现代化。 B) 它们引入了最前沿的店面布局。 C) 它们提高了所售食品的质量。 D) 它们彻底改变了商品分销方式。

questions.q: What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach?
options: They modernized traditional groceries in many ways.
They introduced cutting-edge layout of their stores.
They improved the quality of the food they sold.
They revolutionized the distribution of goods.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach? 问超市靠 这一做法"做成了什么"，是对原文一个具体结果的核对，属细节题。

【拆句】What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach? 主干是"超市做 了什么"，by adopting... 是 by + 动名词的方式状语，表示"通过采用福特式工厂做法这一 手段"，by 在此不是"被"而是"通过"，基础薄弱者易误读，点明即可。 48. What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach? A) They modernized traditional groceries in many ways. B) They introduced cutting-edge layout of their stores. C) They improved the quality of the food they sold. D) They revolutionized the distribution of goods.

【定位】The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food. Supermarkets may not feel cutting- edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time. 超市模仿了讲求效率与标准化的福特式工厂，并把它重新设想成一个买食物的地方。超市如 今也许感觉不再前沿，但它们在当时是分销领域的一场革命。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只说超市模仿福特工厂、成为分销革命，没说它"在许多方面把传统杂货店现代 化"；modernized traditional groceries in many ways 是原文未提的笼统说法。 B) 与原文相反 原文紧接着说超市 may not feel cutting-edge now（如今未必前沿），且布局九十年 几乎没变，并非"引入了前沿布局"；cutting-edge layout 与原文意思相反。 C) 无中生有 原文谈的是分销方式的革命，全程未涉及"食品质量"的提升；improved the quality of the food 在原文找不到任何依据。 D) ✓ 正确 a revolution in distribution ↔They revolutionized the distribution of goods. 预判核心是"在分销上掀起革命"，四项里只有 They revolutionized the distribution of goods. 与定位句 a revolution in distribution 直接等值，故锁定。 典型的超市布局旨在做什么? A) 激发顾客购买鲜花、水果和蔬菜的欲望。 B) 为顾客提供便捷途径获取他们想购买的商品。 C) 诱导顾客进行更多计划外购买。 D) 使顾客获得更愉快的购物体验。

questions.q: What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do?
options: Arouse customers' appetite to buy flowers, fruit and vegetables.
Provide customers easy access to items they want to buy.
Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases.
Enable customers to have a more enjoyable shopping experience.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do? 问布局的具体意图，是对 原文一处目的陈述的核对，属细节题。

【拆句】What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do? 主干是"布局意在做什么"，be intended to do 是"被设计用来做……"的固定结构，是被动语态，主语 layout 是被设计的 对象，看懂这个被动是解题前提，结构上无其他陷阱。

【定位】Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you'll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way. 与此同时，超市把牛奶、鸡蛋等日用必需品全放在最里面，好让你穿过尽可能多的店面，一 路上被诱惑。 49. What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do? A) Arouse customers' appetite to buy flowers, fruit and vegetables. B) Provide customers easy access to items they want to buy. C) Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases. D) Enable customers to have a more enjoyable shopping experience.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 原文说前端摆鲜花果蔬只是 a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite（唤起食 欲）的一个手段，最终目的是让人走遍全店；appetite to buy flowers, fruit and vegetables 把局部手段当成了整体布局的意图。 B) 与原文相反 原文布局恰恰把必需品放到最里、逼顾客绕远，并非"方便顾客买想买的东西"；easy access to items they want to buy 与原文意图相反。 C) ✓ 正确 travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way ↔ Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases. 预判核心是"让顾客多走多买计划外的东西"，四项里只有 Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases. 抓住了布局的真实意图，故锁定。 D) 无中生有 原文讲的是诱导顾客多买，从未说布局是为"让购物更愉快"；more enjoyable shopping experience 是原文没有的说法。 人们长期以来对超市有什么担忧? A) 它们使用狡猾的策略来促进业务。 B) 它们将完全取代当地杂货店。 C) 它们对陈列的商品施加企业黑魔法。 D) 它们利用女性购物者的弱点。

questions.q: What have people long feared about supermarkets?
options: They use tricky strategies to promote their business.
They are going to replace the local groceries entirely.
They apply corporate black magic to the goods on display.
They take advantage of the weaknesses of women shoppers.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What have people long feared about supermarkets? 问人们长期害怕的具体内 容，是对原文一处陈述的核对，属细节题。

【拆句】What have people long feared about supermarkets? 主干是"人们长期害怕超市什么"， have long feared 是现在完成时夹一个副词 long，强调"长久以来一直害怕"，about supermarkets 是 fear 的对象，结构清楚无陷阱。

【定位】We have long feared that this "revolution in distribution" uses corporate black magic on our appetite. 长期以来我们一直害怕，这场"分销革命"在用企业的黑魔法操纵我们的食欲。 50. What have people long feared about supermarkets? A) They use tricky strategies to promote their business. B) They are going to replace the local groceries entirely. C) They apply corporate black magic to the goods on display. D) They take advantage of the weaknesses of women shoppers.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 uses corporate black magic on our appetite ↔ They use tricky strategies to promote their business. 预判核心是"用隐秘手段操纵食欲"，四项里只有 They use tricky strategies to promote their business. 把"黑魔法"这一比喻还原为"狡猾手段"，与定位句契合，故 锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文讲的是人们怕超市操纵食欲，全程未提"取代本地杂货店"；replace the local groceries entirely 是原文没有的内容。 C) 偷换概念 原文是黑魔法用在 our appetite（我们的食欲）上，而 black magic to the goods on display 把作用对象偷换成"陈列的商品"，对象张冠李戴。 D) 以偏概全 关于女性的内容出自被引用的《隐形说客》一书、只是个例证，并非人们"长期"害怕的 核心；weaknesses of women shoppers 拿书中一个局部例子当成了普遍的担忧。
